open_points.subject: ServiceCredential expiry representation
open_points.text: “Any expiry is accepted and stored as supplied … never converted” conflicts with A28: “Persisted timestamps are UTC, stored as offset-naive datetimes.”
open_points.question: When expires_at includes a non-UTC offset, must issuance normalize the instant to offset-naive UTC, preserve the supplied offset, or discard the offset while preserving its wall-clock value?
options: Normalize the instant to offset-naive UTC
Strip the offset without adjusting the wall-clock value
open_points.default_guess: Normalize the instant to offset-naive UTC.

witness.initial: An active service principal exists; current time is 09:00 UTC.
events: An administrator issues a credential with expires_at 12:00+02:00.
The producer authenticates with it at 10:30 UTC.
outcomes: Normalization stores 10:00 UTC, so authentication rejects the credential as expired.
Preserving the 12:00 wall-clock value as a naive timestamp leaves the credential usable until 12:00 UTC.
witness.observer: The producer authenticating with the credential.

open_points.subject: HealthStatus response representation
open_points.text: “liveness at /health/live and readiness at /health/ready, each answering exactly HealthStatus” names HealthStatus but no text defines its fields or JSON encoding.
open_points.question: What exact successful HTTP body and content type must each health endpoint return?
options: A JSON object with a status string, such as {"status":"ok"}
A JSON object with a boolean, such as {"ok":true}

witness.initial: The runtime application starts with valid settings and an available database.
witness.observer: The health monitor parsing the responses.

open_points.subject: Health endpoint request methods
open_points.text: “liveness at /health/live and readiness at /health/ready” fixes the paths but does not fix the accepted HTTP methods.
open_points.question: Which HTTP methods are accepted at the liveness and readiness paths, including whether HEAD is supported?
open_points.default_guess: Accept GET and HEAD, with HEAD returning the GET headers and no body.

witness.initial: The runtime application is running normally.
outcomes: The endpoint accepts HEAD and returns a successful status with no body.
The endpoint rejects HEAD with method not allowed.
witness.observer: The load balancer performing the readiness check.

open_points.subject: Readiness storage-failure response
open_points.text: “when that cannot be opened it answers 500 with no HealthStatus body and no internal detail” does not fix whether the response body is empty or contains a generic non-HealthStatus error, nor its content type.
open_points.question: What exact body, headers and content type must readiness return when opening the database transaction fails?
options: A fixed generic JSON error without internal detail
A fixed generic text response without internal detail
open_points.default_guess: Return an empty 500 response with the standard security headers.

witness.initial: The application is running, but its SQLite database cannot be opened.
outcomes: The response is HTTP 500 with an empty body.
The response is HTTP 500 with a fixed generic body such as {"status":"unavailable"}.
witness.observer: The health monitor and any proxy interpreting the failure response.
